How to become seriously
well-read in your 20s
Keep a book on you at all times. On the bus, in waiting rooms, at lunch. Twenty minutes of dead time a day is around fifteen books a year.
Mix old and new. One classic, then one modern book, then a biography. Variety gives you a wider view than reading only one kind of book.
Read about places before you visit them. A city's history, its famous people, its food. Travel becomes ten times richer when you know the story.
Join or start a small reading group. Three friends, one book a month, one dinner to discuss it. Talking about books with friends makes the ideas stick far longer than reading alone.
Learn a little every day. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it fills the gaps that books leave between them.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It fills the gaps that books leave between them.

slides.texte_overlay: Underline and write in the margins. Arguing with a book makes you think. A marked-up book is a book you actually understood.
Don't finish books you hate. Life is short. Drop a boring book after fifty pages and pick up one that excites you. Loving reading matters most.
